name: Power generation and fuel
sells: firm electricity and the fuel behind it (gas turbines and gas supply; nuclear restarts and uprates; solar with batteries; on-site generation)
summary: Every GPU-hour is a kilowatt-hour first. New firm capacity in the United States is gated by gas turbine order books, fuel delivery and permitting, not by demand.

name: Grid, interconnection and transformers
sells: a connection that can deliver the power to a site: transmission, substations, transformers and switchgear
summary: A generator and a data centre are only useful once connected. Interconnection queues, transformer lead times and utility planning cycles set the pace.

name: Data centre shell and cooling
sells: a building with power, cooling and networking ready for racks, sold as capacity by the megawatt
summary: Land, permits, water and cooling capacity turn connected megawatts into rack-ready megawatts. Density is rising with liquid cooling.

name: Wafers and advanced packaging
sells: leading-edge logic wafers and the CoWoS packaging that joins a GPU die to its memory
summary: One foundry makes every leading AI accelerator and its packaging capacity has been the tightest link since 2023.

name: Memory and storage (HBM, DRAM, NAND)
sells: high-bandwidth memory stacked on each GPU, server DRAM, and the NAND behind enterprise SSDs
summary: Three suppliers of HBM; wafer capacity moved to HBM starves DRAM and NAND. Where prices moved first in 2025.

name: GPUs, servers, racks and networking
sells: accelerators assembled into servers and racks with the network that ties them into a cluster
summary: The unit everyone counts. Price per GPU, GPUs per rack and rack power decide what a megawatt is worth.

name: GPU-hours
sells: rented accelerator time under multi-year contracts (neoclouds) or used internally (hyperscalers)
summary: Where the top-down company models live. The price of a GPU-hour is the hinge between the physical chain and the dollar chain.

name: Tokens
sells: model output sold by the million tokens, trained and served on rented or owned GPU-hours
summary: Throughput per GPU and price per million tokens decide how the GPU-hour dollar splits between owner and lab.

name: Applications and end demand
unit: tokens consumed per user per day
sells: products that turn tokens into revenue, split by how much compute each consumes
summary: Who pays, how much, and how many tokens each dollar of revenue burns. The demand that has to justify everything upstream.
